basis: Renal phosphate wasting causes hypophosphatemia and rickets; dentin defects and tooth abscesses occur in 30-79%. Nephrocalcinosis is often treatment related.
Isolated spermatogenic failure with abnormal sperm morphology and motility; no established endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease.
Myotonia and chondrodysplasia define the disease. Visual impairment and intellectual disability are annotated at 80-99%; cataracts at 30-79%.
Monogenic diabetes caused by impaired pancreatic insulin secretion; no common direct extra-endocrine damage established for this subtype.
Cleft lip/palate affects oral structures; tetraphocomelia is a congenital malformation of all four limbs.
Congenital junctional tachyarrhythmia; associated cardiomyopathy remains within the cardiovascular axis.
Congenital tricuspid valve malformation. Respiratory insufficiency reflects cardiac physiology; stroke and other extracardiac injury are uncommon.
Inflammatory inner-ear disease affecting hearing and balance; the umbrella includes infectious, traumatic and toxic causes without a uniform immune mechanism.
Benign neoplasm arising from sebaceous glands of the skin.
Inherited dystrophies confined to the corneal epithelium, basement membrane and superficial stroma.
Congenital skeletal muscle disease with type II fiber atrophy; respiratory failure in 2/2 is attributed to muscle weakness rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Benign tumor of the nasal cavity, which belongs to the upper respiratory tract.
Inherited thrombotic microangiopathy is defined by small-vessel thrombosis, hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and renal injury.
B-lymphoblast malignancy involving blood/marrow; the leukemia/lymphoma classification also supports the lymphoma mechanism axis.
Microcornea, myopia and chorioretinal atrophy occurred in 8/8 patients; external ear positioning does not establish otologic dysfunction.
UV-induced skin disease; microphthalmia and neurodevelopmental impairment each reported in 1/3, with cataract also documented. Occasional ataxia alone would not qualify.
Polyp confined to the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the specified axes.
Malignant tumor originating in the parietal pleura; pleura belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; nystagmus, diplopia and dysphagia reflect neurologic dysfunction without established direct eye or gastrointestinal injury.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dysfunction, heart failure and arrhythmias.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with motor neuron/axonal dysfunction; weakness and nystagmus do not establish separate intrinsic muscle or eye damage.
Secondary cardiomyopathy is defined by cardiac dysfunction; its varied causes do not establish another organ axis across the umbrella.
Oral, digital and retinal malformations define the syndrome; intellectual disability is also a defining feature, with brain atrophy reported; frequency unquantified.
Immune-mediated ulcerative colitis confined to the left colon; no common direct extraintestinal damage established for this concept.
Named syndrome defined by microcephaly, cataract and hearing loss; growth retardation alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine damage.
